item.title: BUSINESS BRIEFS: South Mountain Concerts names Executive Director; Berkshire Community Land Trust names Executive Director; Berkshire Community College staffing updates; WAM Theatre welcomes directors; Flying Cloud announces directors; Berkshire Innovation Center appoints directors; Lee Chamber of Commerce announces officers and directors
item.description: South Mountain Concerts has announced Lydia Chernicoff as its next Executive Director.

item.title: CAPITAL IDEAS: How the rich avoid taxes, and you can, too (2026 update)
item.description: Tax planning is not only about April 15, it is also about what happens to assets when you’re not around to sign the return.

item.title: TECH & INNOVATION: Freedom without continuity becomes noise
item.description: We have built an economy of options and a culture of pivots. What we have not built is the patience for anything that takes long enough to matter.

item.title: Boston Symphony Orchestra and New England Conservatory launch landmark ‘BSO x NEC Alliance’
item.description: Through an integrated approach to artist cultivation, content development, and shared use of campuses and venues, this first-of-its-kind alliance between a major symphony orchestra and a leading conservatory will fuel innovation and excellence in orchestral music in Boston and beyond.

item.title: BUSINESS MONDAY: Spotlight on HappyPlace Berkshires in Great Barrington
item.description: An artist-entrepreneur transforms Berkshire pride into locally made screenprints and other branded merchandise, building community one iconic design at a time.

item.title: W.E.B Du Bois event on February 23 moving to Zoom
item.description: The event has been moved to Zoom due to the snowstorm.

item.title: Berkshire Food Co-op facing financial trouble
item.description: Members of the Co-op’s Board Of Directors and its general manager avoided directly answering questions concerning the Co-op’s finances, including whether it is in danger of closing.

item.title: FILM REVIEW: Fatih Akin’s ‘Amrum’
item.description: It is the last days of World War II, with Berlin about to fall. We see the world through the eyes of a sensitive, thoughtful 12-year-old boy, Nanning, whose mother and father are committed Nazis and who still wears his Hitler Youth uniform.

item.title: STEPHEN COHEN: The Black Magus
item.description: I am always struck by our contradictions—how we interpret, invoke, and discard or simply ignore concepts of morality.
